name: Munit
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Semi-phonemic wordlist, no stress marks; intro p. viii (p. 8) notes only 'The Munit language has a series of nasalised vowels.'

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: p. 6 (p. 14), general to the whole survey: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Munit (abbr. MUN, listed under Astrolabe Bay) gets no language-specific stress remark.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. n.d. Munit Swadesh List (archive.org item rosettaproject_mtc_swadesh-1).
sources.note: Wordlist only (nasalised vowels, length, glottal stop transcribed); no stress.

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, Munit language page (data from Z'graggen 1980).
sources.note: Lexicon only; sole cited source is Z'graggen 1980; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Village index p. 52: Berin (150), Bemari (53), Oupan (94) are Munit C3 villages — fixes the identity of 'Berin phonology'.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Munit appears only in comparative pronoun/lexical tables.
Stub; no phonology; only reference is Z'graggen 1980.

sources.citation: SIL PNG Branch. n.d. [file dated 2004]. Organised Phonology Data: Munit (Berin) Language [MTC], Madang - Madang Province. Ukarumpa: SIL. 4 pp. Unpublished manuscript, SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42414.

tone.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress occurs on either first or second syllable, but has not been analysed properly yet.

sources.note: PARADISEC/DataCite describe it as Z'graggen's handwritten Munit comparative-wordlist notebook (page scan), i.e. the field manuscript underlying the published Z'graggen 1980 D-32 Munit list (a work listed here); nothing about tone or stress is visible in the record, and whether the phonetic field transcription carries pitch/stress marks can only be checked by a registered PARADISEC user.
